deviations: dictionary_new: A table of at least DICTMINSZ slots, in a Vec; it grows with dictionary::grow, as the static dictionary_grow did.
dictionary_del: A Dictionary frees its entries when it is dropped.
dictionary_get: None for a missing key and Some(None) for a key without value, where the C returned the default or NULL.
dictionary_set: Keys and values are copied into the table, as the static xstrdup copied them.
iniparser_set_error_callback: A load reports its errors to the report function it is given (parse, load), as LoadError values; LoadError::message is the text the default callback wrote to stderr.
iniparser_getsecname: The slot of the section, whose key is its name.
iniparser_dumpsection_ini: The C wrote the section name into a 1025-byte buffer, which a longer name overflowed; it is written in full now.
iniparser_getsecnkeys: The number of the slots it returns.
iniparser_getseckeys: The slots of the keys, in place of the C's array of key pointers.
iniparser_getlongint: A key without value (a section) reads as an empty value, 0; the C passed NULL to strtol.
iniparser_getint: A key without value (a section) reads as an empty value, 0; the C passed NULL to strtol.
iniparser_getdouble: atof in the C locale; a hexadecimal value of more than 16 digits may round differently in its last bit. A key without value reads as an empty value, 0; the C passed NULL to atof.
iniparser_getboolean: A key without value (a section) is no boolean; the C read through NULL.
iniparser_set: Lowercasing is ASCII's (lowercase, as the static strlwc did in the C locale).
iniparser_load: The file is read whole, then parsed as fgets read it line by line; parse_line is the static iniparser_line, strip the static strstrip.
iniparser_freedict: A Dictionary frees its entries when it is dropped.

tap:tests/codecoremorph_characterization/iniparser_2_test/dump_lists_every_entry_of_a_grown_dictionary: The C read the struct's size field; the Rust test reads Slots::size. The C checked that the memory stream opened; dump's Result stands for it.

tap:tests/codecoremorph_characterization/iniparser_test/dump_writes_nothing_for_an_empty_or_null_dictionary: A NULL dictionary has no Rust counterpart (the API takes a reference); the NULL stream is a sink, whose dump must succeed.

tap:tests/codecoremorph_characterization/iniparser_test/dump_ini_prints_keys_as_they_are_when_no_section_exists: A NULL dictionary has no Rust counterpart (the API takes a reference); the NULL stream is a sink, whose dump must succeed.

claude.result:
The whole port is done: the iniparser C library is now Rust, built and tested by Cargo alone. All 5 units of the plan are committed on `codecoremorph/20261116-202816-8c54`, and the final clean build ran 52 tests and passed. The full report is at `E:\codecoremorph-trials\c-eval\iniparser\.codecoremorph\runs\20261116-202816-8c54\report.md`.

Before planning, the run asked for tests on three dump functions no test covered. I wrote 20 characterization tests in two jobs; all 20 were accepted and committed first (`bf0910ea64ff`).

| Unit | What it did | Attempts | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| U-0001 | Ported `src/dictionary.c` to `iniparser_rs::dictionary` and deleted the C file | 1 | `0a16eab8b2df` |
| U-0002 | Ported `src/iniparser.c` to `iniparser_rs::iniparser`; no C had to stay | 2 | `dad0bc9122d4` |
| U-0003 | Turned the 10 tests of `iniparser_2_test.c` into Rust tests | 1 | `4e27cd71a54a` |
| U-0004 | Turned the 10 tests of `iniparser_test.c` into Rust tests | 1 | `bc71295a24d9` |
| U-0005 | Deleted the C, the headers, the Make build and the temporary C↔Rust glue | 1 | `7a72406e729c` |

U-0002's first attempt failed only at the interface check: the tool that generates the C header couldn't read one function-pointer type. Spelling the type out fixed it. The finished crate has no `unsafe` code.

**Things you should know:**
- **The project's own tests needed a workaround during the port.** The 20 CuTest tests in `test/` include the `.c` files directly to test private (static) functions. To keep them running against the Rust code until the C was removed, I added small temporary C files under `rust/c-whitebox/` and test-only exports in the glue. All of it was deleted in the last unit. U-0005 then rewrote those 20 tests as Rust tests (`test_dictionary.rs`, `test_iniparser.rs`), which now stand in for `make check`.
- **`make check` never failed on a CuTest failure** (the test runner always exits 0). I read its summary after each port instead: `OK (20 tests)` each time.
- **I approved two commits the tool held for review:**
  - In U-0003, one Rust test makes 5 checks where the C made 6. The missing one checked that an in-memory stream opened; in Rust that's the dump's result, which the test unwraps, so a failed write still fails the test.
  - In U-0005, the retirement deleted the C tests' helper header, as it is meant to.
- **Behavior differs only where the C was undefined:**
  - Reading a section (a key with no value) as a number or boolean now gives 0 or "not found" instead of dereferencing NULL.
  - A section name over 1023 bytes no longer overflows a buffer in the ini dump.
  - Lowercasing is ASCII only.
  - The report lists every such note.
- **New in the Rust API:** `iniparser::load`. In C, opening the file and parsing it happened inside `iniparser_load`, and that step had no Rust equivalent once the C was gone.

**What wasn't covered:**
- No tests were excused or flaky, and no unit was skipped or left out.
- `example/`, `doc/` and `html/` were excluded by the manifest and are untouched; the C examples there no longer have a library to build against.
- The README and other docs outside the port still describe the C/Make build.

To review: `git diff 0a38e85 codecoremorph/20261116-202816-8c54`, or `git log` on that branch. Merging is up to you.

I can also turn this summary into a shareable page if it would help.
